correctness.rationale: Exact line-section quadratic completion yields the correctly brightness-weighted conditional survival integral. Sphere disintegration and scaling hard coordinates by sqrt(s) give an integrable beta-ball limit with power (2d-m-r-1)/2 and the exact gamma constant. Uniformity for bounded spectral-gap ratios follows by common compact domination and parameter continuity. Rescaling sphere soft coordinates proves the multivariate large-gap constant; scaling all vanishing axes proves the intermediate matching law. The planar independent quadrature checker passed 5 ratios and the large-ratio coefficient checks. Finite tests alone do not prove the theorem.

value.rationale: A fixed-body long-chord exponent changes when maximal axes collide, leaving the previously quantified fixed-gap law nonuniform and unsuitable for resolving finite chord deficits. The theorem completely resolves this boundary layer with a universal multivariate profile and exact separate limits, exposing how several simultaneous spectral mergers join different power-law exponents. This directly answers a natural geometric probability question about noncommuting limits and supplies structural information absent from the earlier fixed-body classification.
